get.description: Any authenticated role. Returns the signed-in account.

patch.description: Any authenticated role, own account only. Accepts name and phone fields only — permitRole, active and email are not settable here.

get.description: Safety officer only. Filter by permitRole and active state; search spans first name, last name and email.

post.description: Safety officer creates a contractor/inspector/safety_officer account. Public self-registration is disabled for this system.

get.description: Safety officer only. Includes the contractor business profile when the account is a contractor.

patch.description: Safety officer only. Also the deactivation path — send { "active": false }. There is no DELETE: accounts are deactivated, never deleted. Refuses with 409 LAST_SAFETY_OFFICER if the change would leave no active safety officer.

post.description: Contractor registers a worker they send onto site. Answers 409 WORKER_ALREADY_EXISTS when the name collides with one they have already registered.

get.description: Role-scoped: contractor sees own registered workers; safety_officer/inspector see all.

patch.description: Contractor updates one of their own workers. A rename propagates to every certificate, permit row and entrant event by reference.

delete.description: Soft-deletes: the worker leaves suggestions and the default list, and stays readable on every permit and certificate that references them. There is no hard delete.

get.description: One worker with their certificates and the permits they appear on. Contractor sees only their own; safety_officer/inspector see any worker and the full permit history across contractors.

post.description: Contractor registers a safety certificate for one of their workers.

get.description: Role-scoped: contractor sees own registered certificates; safety_officer/inspector see all.

patch.description: Plain overwrite of the fields sent. Certificates are reference data — there is no version history and `deletedAt` remains the retirement path.

get.description: One certificate. Role-scoped like the list: a contractor reads only their own.
Used by the entry-check flow to validate a worker's certificate expiry. Scoped: a contractor may only ask about their own workers.

post.description: Safety officer uploads the image for a new facility plan version. Returns the storage filePath to pass to POST /v1/facility-plans.

get.description: The single currently active plan version, or null if none has ever been activated. Every role may read this — the contractor needs it to place a pin while drafting.

post.description: Safety officer registers a new (inactive) facility plan version from an already-uploaded, already-cropped image. Activate separately with POST /:id/activate.

get.description: All plan versions, newest first. Every role may read this.

post.description: Makes this version the single active plan. The frame is frozen from here on — no crop or edit route exists once a version is activated. Older versions stay retained and resolvable by id.

get.description: One plan version by id, active or not. Every role may read this so a frozen permit can always resolve the version it was placed on.

post.description: Contractor proposes a new area. Created PENDING — unusable by any permit until a safety officer approves it with POST /:id/approve.

get.description: All areas, newest first, optionally filtered by status. Every role may read this. With AREA_VISIBILITY_SCOPED=TRUE a contractor sees only the approved areas they created plus areas granted to them (POST /v1/areas/:id/grants); safety_officer and inspector always see every area. Unset (the default) means every role sees every area.

post.description: Safety officer approves a PENDING area into the master list. Only an APPROVED area may be referenced by a permit.
Safety officer rejects a PENDING area with a required reason. There is no revise-in-place — a corrected proposal is a fresh POST /v1/areas.

Safety officer makes one area visible to one contractor who did not propose it (wayfinder 044). Idempotent — re-granting refreshes who granted it, it never duplicates. Grants only take effect when the deployment sets AREA_VISIBILITY_SCOPED=TRUE; until then every contractor already sees every approved area, and seeding grants first is the intended order. A grant affects the contractor area LIST only: it never widens or narrows the AREA_NOT_APPROVED guard, the overlapping-permit warning, or any officer/inspector view.

get.description: The contractors one area has been explicitly granted to, newest first (wayfinder 044). Drives the officer's grant/revoke screen. It does NOT list the area's proposer — a contractor already sees the areas they created, so no grant exists for that case.

delete.description: Safety officer withdraws one contractor's visibility of one area (wayfinder 044). Idempotent — revoking a grant that is already gone answers 200. Revoking never affects a permit that already references the area: it still saves, still autosaves and still shows its area, because the AREA_NOT_APPROVED guard tests the area's status, not its visibility.

get.description: One area by id, any status. Every role may read this.
Field-facing scan endpoint (rate-limited). Always returns live permit status, never a snapshot from issuance time.

post.description: Contractor creates a new work permit draft (DRAFT status).

get.description: Role-scoped: contractor sees own permits only; safety_officer/inspector see all, optionally filtered by contractorId.

patch.description: Contractor updates their own permit while it is DRAFT or REJECTED. A PENDING permit may also be edited by its own contractor — the edit atomically withdraws it back to DRAFT, so it must be resubmitted.

get.description: Full permit detail including JSA steps, workers, photos, and latest safety reading.

post.description: Re-validates safety-check ranges and worker certificates server-side, then sets the permit to PENDING and notifies safety officers/inspectors. A validation failure answers 400 with EVERY failure listed — `failures[]` for safety readings (same item shape as `validationSummary.failures`) and `certificateFailures[]` for workers — while `errorCode` stays the first failing code.
Safety officer approves a PENDING permit: re-validates readings, issues the QR, sets ACTIVE.

Safety officer rejects a PENDING permit with a required reason and a required typed e-signature (matching approve); the contractor can revise and resubmit. Both are written to the append-only PERMIT_REJECTED audit row. A body missing either field is a 400 with no errorCode.
Hot Work only. Starts the mandatory 30-minute Fire Watch countdown (status -> FIRE_MONITOR).

Closure is the Foreman's action, so a `contractor` may close their OWN permit (a contractor closing someone else's gets a 403 with no errorCode); a `safety_officer` may close any permit. 403 ENTRANTS_STILL_INSIDE if a Confined Space entrant is still checked in; 403 FIRE_WATCH_NOT_ELAPSED if Hot Work's countdown has not finished.
Records an entrant check-in/out. Denies entry (403 CERT_EXPIRED/CERT_MISSING) and writes a CERT_BLOCKED audit entry when the worker's certificate has lapsed.

get.description: Workers currently checked in (their most recent scan event is IN).

post.description: Inspector logs a periodic atmosphere reading. Accepts offlineClientId for idempotent offline replay.

get.description: Most recent first. `overdue` is true if the last reading is older than the facility re-test interval.
Returns a signed token for an ACTIVE/FIRE_MONITOR permit. The frontend renders the QR client-side.
Newest first. Contractor may only view their own permit's trail; safety_officer/inspector may view any.
Safety officer only. Facility-wide, filterable by action and date range.
Role-scoped (and per-user where targetUserId is set), unread-first.

post.description: Marks a role-wide or per-user notification as read for the current user.

get.description: Counts by status, 7-day facility activity, and certs expiring soon. Single endpoint, safe to poll.

post.description: Replays queued entrant-scan/gas-log actions idempotently by clientId. Never aborts the whole batch on one item's failure — each item reports its own success/conflict/error.
